correctness.rationale: A universal upper bound 12 follows because the Witt S(5,8,24) property inserts any five consecutive labels into a weight-eight octad containing at least four consecutive edges. The direct pair-weight identity then gives at most 12. The explicit 24-coordinate ordering was verified against all 759 octads: induced-edge multiplicities 30,118,240,234,137 for 0..4; every weight-eight word therefore has pair weight >=12. Golay weights 12,16,24 cannot lower the bound (pair >=13,17,24). The packaged independent direct pair enumerator, exhaustive 4096-word generation, and unique 42504-pentad checks all returned VERIFY_OK. No extrapolation is involved.

originality.rationale: This is an exact global coordinate-order optimization for extended Golay in a cyclic overlapping-pair channel. Chapman supplies the Golay/Witt structure but no pair-order optimum. Cassuto-Blaum introduces the metric; Yaakobi-Bruck-Siegel studies cyclic-code lower bounds; Chen studies permuted-coordinate covering problems, none directly implies this maximum or contains an attaining order in the inspected materials. Three actual semantic database queries and direct Golay/pair/octad literature searches did not return an equivalent stronger result; unindexed prior work and inaccessible full Cassuto-Blaum text remain risks.

value.rationale: Symbol-pair channels are motivated by overlapping reads in storage. A coordinate permutation can change the pair distance of a fixed error-correcting code, so optimizing it is a natural, nontrivial code-layout invariant. The result globally classifies the optimum for the exceptional [24,12,8] Golay code, improving over generic pair Singleton bound 14 by a structural sharp 12 ceiling, and supplies a concrete witness meeting a design-theoretic obstruction. The claim is neither a textbook Hamming-weight calculation nor a mere small-table recomputation; it is an exact max-min optimization over 24! orderings with a novel constructive matching bound.
